[2023 fall ms applied — problem 4]

Three fertilizers $\times$ three seed types, 45 plots (5 replicates per combination). ANOVA SS: Seed 16.962, Fertilizer 11.820, Seed:Fertilizer 47.949, Residuals 45.210. (1) Give the degrees of freedom. (2) Test that the fertilizer effect is the same regardless of seed type (no interaction). (3) Test that fertilizer has no effect, for every seed type.

response.text:
Let

\[
Y_{ijk}=\mu+\alpha_i+\beta_j+(\alpha\beta)_{ij}+\varepsilon_{ijk},
\]

where \(i=1,2,3\) indexes seed type, \(j=1,2,3\) indexes fertilizer, and \(k=1,\dots,5\). Assume the usual fixed-effects two-way ANOVA model with iid \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) errors.

## (1) Degrees of freedom

There are \(3\times 3\times 5=45\) observations, so total df \(=45-1=44\).

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{Source} & \text{SS} & \text{df} & \text{MS} \\
\hline
\text{Seed} & 16.962 & 3-1=2 & 16.962/2=8.481 \\
\text{Fertilizer} & 11.820 & 3-1=2 & 11.820/2=5.910 \\
\text{Seed:Fertilizer} & 47.949 & (3-1)(3-1)=4 & 47.949/4=11.987 \\
\text{Residual} & 45.210 & 3\cdot 3(5-1)=36 & 45.210/36=1.256 \\
\hline
\text{Total} & 121.941 & 44 & 
\end{array}
\]

## (2) Test for no interaction

The null hypothesis is

\[
H_0:(\alpha\beta)_{ij}=0 \quad \text{for all } i,j,
\]

i.e. the fertilizer effect is the same for every seed type.

Use

\[
F=\frac{MS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}}{MS_E}
=\frac{47.949/4}{45.210/36}.
\]

Thus

\[
F=\frac{11.987}{1.256}\approx 9.545.
\]

Under \(H_0\),

\[
F\sim F_{4,36}.
\]

The p-value is

\[
p=P(F_{4,36}\ge 9.545)\approx 2.3\times 10^{-5}.
\]

So we reject \(H_0\) at any conventional significance level. There is strong evidence of a seed-type by fertilizer interaction: the fertilizer effect depends on seed type.

## (3) Test that fertilizer has no effect for every seed type

The null hypothesis is stronger than “no fertilizer main effect.” It is

\[
H_0:\mu_{i1}=\mu_{i2}=\mu_{i3}
\quad \text{for each seed type } i=1,2,3.
\]

Equivalently, the mean may depend on seed type, but not on fertilizer. Thus we test all terms involving fertilizer jointly:

\[
H_0:\beta_j=0 \text{ and } (\alpha\beta)_{ij}=0.
\]

The numerator sum of squares is therefore

\[
SS_{\text{Fertilizer}}+SS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}}
=11.820+47.949=59.769.
\]

The numerator df is

\[
2+4=6.
\]

So

\[
F=\frac{(SS_{\text{Fertilizer}}+SS_{\text{Seed:Fertilizer}})/6}{MS_E}
=\frac{59.769/6}{45.210/36}.
\]

Thus

\[
F=\frac{9.9615}{1.2558}\approx 7.932.
\]

Under \(H_0\),

\[
F\sim F_{6,36}.
\]

The p-value is

\[
p=P(F_{6,36}\ge 7.932)\approx 1.7\times 10^{-5}.
\]

Therefore we reject \(H_0\). There is strong evidence that fertilizer has an effect for at least one seed type. Because the interaction test in part (2) was also significant, the fertilizer effect appears to vary by seed type.
